reason: Stamp schema_version on history rows so the reader's version guard can fire on the store's own data (#701): module-size 32689->32744 (+55), measured on this tree rebased onto d0970e8. Attributed empirically, not from the arrow. Per #689 the left operand of a check-arch verdict is baselines.json (26965, stale -- tracked in #703), so the 5779 the verdict prints is almost entirely inherited: 5724 of it is already present on the untouched branch point. The real base was obtained by moving .harness/arch/allowances aside (otherwise feat-459's recorded 32689 suppresses the regression and hides the raw number entirely) and re-running `harness check-arch --json` with the three changed source files reverted to origin/main: 32689 exactly, to the digit the same value feat-459 recorded, which is what confirms the base is inherited rather than mine. Restoring the three files and re-running the identical command gives 32744. So this change's own contribution is 55. Attributed further, one file at a time, each reverted alone against the same 32744: ts/src/history/record.ts 32711 (+33, LEGACY_UNVERSIONED_SCHEMA_VERSION and resolveSchemaVersion with the reasoning that stops them being collapsed), ts/src/history/schema.ts 32726 (+18, the stamp in serializeLocalRecord and why it lives there), ts/src/history/ndjson-store.ts 32740 (+4, the guard reading the resolved version). Those three sum to exactly 55, so nothing in the change is unaccounted for. Nothing else in the diff contributes: the two modified test files under ts/src/history/ (ndjson-store.test.ts, schema.test.ts) measure zero -- reverting only the three non-test files with the test edits still in place returns exactly 32689, which is the empirical proof that module-size does not count test code even when it sits under src/ -- and the remainder is CHANGELOG.md, ts/test/write-seam.test.ts and ts/test/fixtures/history-write-golden.json. Of the 73 added source lines, 60 are comment or blank and 13 are code. That ratio is the point rather than an accident. The 13 lines are trivial (one object key, one `??`, two constants); what the file has to carry is the reason, because every part of this fix is one a later reader would otherwise undo: LEGACY_UNVERSIONED_SCHEMA_VERSION is a frozen literal 2 that must NEVER be aliased to SCHEMA_VERSION -- aliasing them re-creates #701 exactly, silently, on the day the version bumps -- and the constants are equal today, so the code alone cannot tell anyone why there are two of them. The same applies to stamping in serializeLocalRecord rather than at the call sites (a writer that must remember the field is the writer that forgot it, which is how #701 happened) and to leaving serializeRun/serializeTestResult unstamped (they map to the remote store's table columns, which have no such field). Splitting would not help -- module-size is a repo-wide aggregate, so N files summing to 55 score identically to one, and all three files stay far under every per-file threshold. Nothing was absorbed here to avoid a fix: newViolations is 0, and totalViolations stays at 20 both with and without the change. Entropy is 283 against a 291 ceiling, unchanged by this branch; both new exports have real callers (resolveSchemaVersion from ndjson-store.ts, LEGACY_UNVERSIONED_SCHEMA_VERSION from the store's own module and its unit suite), no entryPoints entry was declared and maxFindings was not touched. Per #703, this absolute is valid only until the next allowance merges beneath it; the +55 contribution is the durable number and must be re-measured from scratch on rebase, never derived by adding to a previous total.
